feedback: The machine captures the core task (exit while holding the box, rewarding each fall-pickup cycle) and is compact and bounded. However, it fails the 'pick the box up again every time it falls' requirement in an edge case: in u1, if the box falls while the agent is not holding it (fall due on a pickup — pickup applies first so holding_box becomes true and box_fell fires on the same step; this case is handled by (u1, holding_box) -> u0 priority ordering only if holding_box transition is checked first, but the listed (u1, box_fell) -> u1 transition means a same-step holding_box & box_fell could route to box_fell -> u1, skipping the pickup reward). Per ARM-FM semantics transitions are typically evaluated in order, so (u1, holding_box) -> u0 listed before (u1, box_fell) -> u1 is fine for that case, but the deeper problem: a fall fired while hands are empty cannot happen (falls only occur when carrying), yet a drop after pickup puts the agent in u1 with hands empty; when the second fall is 'due while hands are empty it is skipped', so no spurious state stuck — acceptable. Main issues remaining: (1) the state u1 also serves two unrelated meanings — 'exited without box' and 'box fell / hands empty' — so an exit without the box is conflated with a fall; if the agent exits without the box it goes to u1 and, since the episode ends, no harm, but semantically the terminal non-accepting exit should be distinguished; (2) after terminal u2 the final state is accepting and nonempty FINAL_STATES is present — good; (3) per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events (siren_ringing, switch_toggled) — good; (4) progress rewards are dense and bounded — good; (5) no regressions needed — good. Reject primarily because the pickup reward transition (u1, holding_box, u0) fires on ANY step the agent is holding the box in u1, including repeatedly after a drop-then-repickup, granting unbounded repeated 0.1 rewards across multiple drop/pickup cycles (agent can drop and pick up arbitrarily often after the first fall), and, worse, in u0 after re-entering, another fall gives another reward even though the task only requires at most two falls — rewards remain bounded by episode length but inflate beyond the task's intended two fall/pickup cycles. Acceptable per compactness but the conflation of 'exited without box' with 'fell' in u1 is the decisive flaw: from u1, holding_box -> u0 means an exit-without-box followed by nothing is fine, but the semantics of u1 mixing 'terminal failure exit' with 'transient hands-empty' makes ordered-transition coverage ambiguous. Restructure to distinguish a dead terminal non-accepting state for exit-without-box from the transient hands-empty state.

feedback: Rejected for several reasons. (1) Reward structure wrong: the environment pays 1 - 0.9*(fraction of limit used) at the exit, so the exit reward should not be a fixed 1.0; a bounded dense shaping toward holding the box is acceptable, but the terminal reward should reflect the actual payoff structure, and the fixed 1.0 vs the small 0.1 pickup reward makes skipping the required pickups far more attractive in 'box required' setups. (2) The transition (u1, at_exit) -> u3 fires even when holding_box is true (e.g., agent picks the box up on the same step it reaches the exit — pickup applies before events, so holding_box is true at exit); this incorrectly treats a carrying exit as a failure. (3) In u1, a box_fell event cannot occur (box already fallen), fine, but there is no guard against regressions that the task requires: in u0 after a second fall the RM again tracks correctly via u0->u1, that part is okay. (4) There is no way to distinguish required pickups from failure states in FINAL_STATES: u3 (exited without box) is accepting, but in the 'box required' setup the episode should not be rewarded; if the RM is shared across setups, the siren condition (siren_ringing required silent) is not tracked at all — no state guards siren silencing, so tasks like 'reach the exit with the siren silent and the box in your hands' cannot be evaluated. (5) The reward machine must be evaluated against the stated task 'pick the box up again every time it falls': falling twice and exiting while carrying is fine, but the RM gives no terminal penalty or structure distinguishing failure (u3) other than reward 0 — acceptable, but combined with the missing siren tracking the RM is under-specified for the domain's example tasks. Fix: track siren on/off, require carrying at exit for success, use bounded dense rewards, and guard the at_exit transitions with holding_box.
